summary: Implemented a100c/runtime/ as the reusable precompiled C native runtime plus the hand-written assembly operator stub that proves the boundary. a100rt.h declares the single runtime<->generated-code ABI (lp64d psABI conventions, F045): operator_entry signature, a100rt_stage_barrier helper call form, workspace contract (zeroed per call, padded/aligned thread-private regions), stats observation record, and _Static_assert-pinned struct offsets for assembly consumers. bundle.c is the a100-native-io/v1 reader (views with dtype/shape/strides/offset, typed scalars, pointer-table relocations patched on open and restored on close) that validates the whole image before writing any byte, so a format violation is a recorded refusal that never touches the file. pool.c is the persistent pthread pool (1/2/4/8 workers, created once per process, startup-gated so a partial create cannot deadlock, C11 atomics, go/done/stage barriers). main.c parses --bundle/--threads/[--repeats], snapshots the mapped image, restores it before each repeat (independent executions), compares repeat images, and prints one status JSON line (threads, pool_initializations, per-worker guest_tid/items, repeats_all_equal). operator_stub.S (authored here, not pipeline output) reads views/scalars and writes outputs through two structural paths: strided-alias (guest-pointer dereference at index 0, strided stores, typed scalar addend round-tripped through thread-private workspace, stage barrier, shared-slot partial merge, second stage adding the merged total) and bfloat16 value storage (16-bit sign flip). build.py compiles and links exclusively with the declared cross gcc/as/ld and the declared sysroot (F002/F003/F004) into a100c/runtime/build/operator_exec (sha256 4d4ff3dbc3e3154d2592764c663b4925331bc43a3c7bcaf8101781adc1ab5008), caching runtime objects by content digest. Both declared tests pass end to end under the declared QEMU endpoint via a100_support/run-riscv.sh.

evidence: The executed-and-compared artifact is a100c/runtime/build/operator_exec (sha256 4d4ff3dbc3e3154d2592764c663b4925331bc43a3c7bcaf8101781adc1ab5008), built only from a100c/runtime/{a100rt.h,bundle.c,pool.c,main.c,operator_stub.S} by the declared cross toolchain. Every comparison in the smoke test is computed host-side from the case's own inputs (np.array_equal against independently derived expected values), never by the runtime or the stub grading itself. The comparisons can and do fail when the contract is violated: during development the pool2/4/8 checks FAILED while one staged bundle was (incorrectly) reused across thread-count runs, because the second run consumed the first run's outputs -- a recorded failing control demonstrating the comparison observes real state, which was fixed by staging a fresh bundle per execution. The refusal path was exercised with five distinct corruptions (magic, size, view-offset, reloc-entry, garbage), each rejected with a named reason and an untouched file. Pool evidence matches F019: distinct guest tids at 1/2/4/8, full 32771-item coverage, exactly one pool initialization per process, and repeats reuse the same pool (pool_initializations stays 1 across --repeats 3).
